definitions.gloss: fairly; more or less; passable; not bad
definitions.explanation: An understated positive evaluation meaning something is acceptable or reasonably good, though not outstanding. Conveys a reserved, characteristically Japanese form of moderate praise.

examples.japanese: ⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧まずまずだった。
⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出来|でき}→出来：11763_deki⟧だった⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧。
examples.english: I think today's game was a fairly good performance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧にして⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{成績|せいせき}→成績：03379_seiseki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{褒|ほ}められた→褒める：01204_homeru⟧。
examples.english: For a first attempt, it was a passable result, and even the teacher praised me.

notes:
An evaluative adverb indicating something is acceptable or moderately good — not excellent, but satisfactory. Derived from repeating ⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧ (first; at any rate), which itself can mean "reasonably."

USAGE:
- Expresses a mildly positive evaluation — "not perfect but good enough"
- Can function as an adverb modifying a noun with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧: まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧ (passable results)
- Can also be used as a predicate: まずまずだ (it's passable)
- The tone is reserved — it avoids strong praise, which can feel very Japanese in its understatement

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{成績|せいせき}→成績：03379_seiseki⟧: passable grades
- まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{結果|けっか}→結果：02486_kekka⟧: fairly good results
- まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出来|でき}→出来：11763_deki⟧: decent work/performance
- まずまず⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{天気|てんき}→天気：00582_tenki⟧: fairly good weather

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦そこそこ→そこそこ：06684_sokosoko⟧: so-so, moderate — similar but can imply slightly lower evaluation
- ⟦まあまあ→まあまあ：05430_maamaa⟧: so-so, not bad — very similar; ⟦まあまあ→まあまあ：05430_maamaa⟧ is more common in casual speech
- ⟦{悪|わる}くない→悪い：00908_warui⟧: not bad — a direct evaluation rather than hedged praise
